entry.title: A decompressor is an interpreter for hostile input: here's what that costs to ship safely
entry.summary: A compression library is a uniquely dangerous thing to ship. It's small, fast, and dependency-light — which is exactly why it ends up linked into web servers, firmware, package managers, and SSH daemons, sitting in everyone's hot path. When xz was backdoored in early 2024 (CVE-2024-3094, CVSS 10.0), the lesson most people took was "audit your maintainers." Building ZXC, the lesson I took was narrower and more uncomfortable: most of the industry treats a decompressor like a utility function, when it's really an interpreter for attacker-controlled input. entry.summary: I've been watching the LLM gateway benchmarks get faster. Bifrost at 11 microseconds, Helicone at 8 milliseconds, LiteLLM at 8ms.
